items.q: Should founders chase AI products or use AI for something else?
items.a: Hormozi is an AI advocate who says most founders use it wrong: building products the models will swallow, **automating non-constraints** (e.g. $350K to replace $11K/mo VAs when the business is demand-constrained), and **outsourcing hard thinking**. Use AI for **execution speed**; compare Claude/OpenAI on the same decision, then **own the call**.

items.q: Why is delegating hard judgment to models so dangerous?
items.a: "Do not delegate the hardest thinking work you have, because you will just get so **weak so fast**." Outsourcing thinking causes **atrophy**. A simple filter for AI-maxing founders: **are you making more money?**

items.q: What still wins when AI floods content supply?
items.a: **Reality is the moat.** As AI floods supply against stagnant demand, **brand, reputation, live/IRL proof, and track record** beat polished generic output. Advertise the **customer outcome**, not "we're an AI company."

items.q: Why fix retention before pouring money into distribution?
items.a: Two $3M businesses look the same until one must **replace all customers yearly** — a "hole in the back of the bus." **Retention before distribution**; sticky revenue compounds when distribution arrives. Strong marketing **amplifies product flaws**.

items.q: Why isn't the fastest path to $10M the same as $100M?
items.a: **Time-horizon foundation design**: the fastest path to $1M / $10M / $100M are **different builds** (block-tower exercise). "The fastest way to build a $10 million business is not the fastest way to build a **$100 million business**."

Concrete start: **LLC, bank, payments**, then ask a stranger for money — the **first-dollar identity shift**. Early fear is usually **specific judgment fear** (name the 1–2 people), not amorphous "people."

items.q: How does Hormozi think about value and pricing?
items.a: Value equation: **outcome × perceived likelihood / time delay × effort/sacrifice**. Use **Van Westendorp** four-question pricing before launch; in services, **price is a capability signal**. Price up when demand exceeds supply while still over-delivering.

items.q: When should you pivot vs push through?
items.a: **Thesis-invalidation pivot rule**: pivot when a **core assumption is disproven**; push when the thesis holds but progress is slow. Channel existing desire — "We don't want to create demand. We want to **channel it**." Specialize after survival (~$1–3M), not before.

sections.title: Adversity and what business can't buy

items.q: How should you respond when adversity hits?
items.a: Map **adversity-response vectors**: tolerance depth, fall depth, recovery speed, adaptation direction. "My **emotional discomfort** is not an adequate reason to change what I'm doing." Reject performative grief — suffering intensity is **not proof of love**.

items.q: Does Hormozi sell entrepreneurship as a happiness path?
items.a: No — he sells **quantitative business outcomes**, not happiness from success. Best financial decision he names: marrying **Leila Hormozi**.
